items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower and its residue functors
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked cyclotomic PBW/Skryabin and category-O single-block suppliers; the explicit finite spectral and centre computations below introduce no additional choice.

Fix a nonempty set $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ of consecutive integers (possibly all of
$\mathbb Z$ or half-infinite), put $I^+:=I\cup(I+1)$, fix a level $l\ge1$ and an
integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, and let
$\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^{l}\Lambda_{m_j}\in P^+$ be the corresponding dominant
integral weight. Throughout, the ground field is $\mathbb C$ and the degree-$d$
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra $H_d(m)$ is the algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: the quotient of the degenerate
affine Hecke algebra by the relation $(x_1-m_1)\cdots(x_1-m_l)=0$, with
$\mathbb C$-basis $\{x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w\}$ over $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$,
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}H_d(m)=l^d d!$. The $x_1,\dots,x_d$ commute pairwise.

**(1) Joint spectral idempotents and content idempotents.** For
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in\mathbb Z^d$ let $e(i)\in H_d(m)$ be the joint polynomial
spectral idempotent of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ that projects onto the generalized joint
eigenspace with generalized eigenvalues $i_1,\dots,i_d$; these idempotents are
those of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
they lie in the commutative subalgebra generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$, are
mutually orthogonal, sum to the identity of $H_d(m)$, and all but finitely many
are zero. For $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $d=\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$ put

$$I_\alpha:=\{\,i\in I^d\ :\ \textstyle\sum_{r=1}^{d}\alpha_{i_r}=\alpha\,\},\qquad e_\alpha:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}e(i)\in H_d(m),\qquad H^\Lambda_\alpha:=e_\alpha H_d(m).$$

Because $I_\alpha$ is finite (so only finitely many nonzero $e(i)$ occur in it),
$e_\alpha$ is an idempotent of $H_d(m)$, nonzero or zero, and $H^\Lambda_\alpha$
is a finite-dimensional algebra with identity $e_\alpha$. Its (finite
dimensional, unital) left modules are exactly the $H_d(m)$-modules on which
$e_\alpha$ acts as the identity.

**(2) The supported degree and the tower.** The **degree-$d$ supported tower
algebra** is $f_{I,d}H_d(m)$ with $f_{I,d}:=\sum_{i\in I^d}e(i)$; for
$I\ne\mathbb Z$ this is in general a proper central cut of the whole degree-$d$
algebra $H_d(m)$, and no equality with $H_d(m)$ is asserted. The **tower** is

$$H^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha .$$

It is a unital algebra when $I$ is finite and a locally unital algebra in
general; the ambient tower inclusion is the degree-raising embedding
$\iota\colon H_d(m)\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}(m)$ of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
At level $0$ the tower is concentrated in degree $0$: $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$
and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$.

**(3) Grothendieck groups and the Cartan pairing.** For each $\alpha$ let
$D(A)$ range over representatives of the simple finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules and $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ over their
projective covers. The **module Grothendieck group** $G_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is
the Grothendieck group $G_0$ of the category of finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]])
and the **split projective group** $K_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]); both are taken block
by block and then summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. The **Cartan pairing**

$$\langle-,-\rangle\colon K_0(H^\Lambda)\times G_0(H^\Lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \langle[P],[M]\rangle:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{H^\Lambda}(P,M),$$

is the object-level Hom pairing of
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]; its biadditivity
on the two groups is the descent proved in
[[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]], which also shows
that $\{[Y(A)]\}$ and $\{[D(A)]\}$ are dual bases (over $\mathbb C$ every simple
endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$). Different blocks are orthogonal.

**(4) Residue maps and residue functors.** For $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q^+$
the embedding $\iota$ composed with the projection onto the block
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is the non-unital algebra homomorphism

$$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad u_{\alpha,i}:=\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}(e_\alpha)=\sum_{i\in I_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\ i_{d+1}=i}e(i).$$

The **residue restriction functor** $e_i$ sends a finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$-module $M$ to the vector space
$u_{\alpha,i}M$ viewed as an $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module through
$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$, and the **residue induction functor** $f_i$ sends a
finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module $M$ to
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}M$. Their
well-definedness, exactness, biadjointness, compatibility with the duality
$\circledast$ of (5), and their effect on Grothendieck groups (adjoint operators
for the Cartan pairing, by
[[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]]) are the
content of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]];
summing over $\alpha$ gives endofunctors $e_i,f_i$ of the tower.

**(5) Duality.** The anti-automorphism $\ast$ of $H_d(m)$ with
$s_r^\ast=s_r$ and $x_r^\ast=x_r$ preserves each $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. On
finite-dimensional left $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules put
$M^{\circledast}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(M,\mathbb C)$ with left action
$(hf)(m):=f(h^\ast m)$. This duality fixes every simple module and commutes with
the residue functors; it is the ordinary duality recorded in
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]],
and it is used throughout this page in the form $M^{\circledast}$.

**(6) Stable and admissible data.** A charge datum as above is used in the
form of its admissible stable realization of
[[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]];
stable range means at least $d$ Jordan strings of maximal length $l$, and
admissibility means $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$ for the origin $c$.
These hypotheses are only invoked where the corresponding supplier is used;
the definitions (1)-(5) themselves do not assume them.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inherited Axiom of Choice and a nonempty consecutive set $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$, a level $l\ge1$, an
integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, and the algebra $H_d(m)$ of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] with its commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_d$ satisfying $(x_1-m_1)\cdots(x_1-m_l)=0$ and its isomorphism
$H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$ in the admissible
stable realization supplied by
[[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]]. We prove the
single-block property (b), as announced in the Remarks.

[F5] Pairwise comaximal ideals of a commutative ring satisfy the Chinese
remainder isomorphism $R/\prod_s I_s\cong\prod_s R/I_s$
([[thm-chinese-remainder-theorem-for-comaximal-ideals]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Per-position polynomial projectors and integer spectra.** The finite-dimensional algebra has a faithful regular representation. For adjacent dots put $\delta=x_r-x_{r+1}$ and $\phi_r=s_r\delta+1$. The native cross relations give $\phi_rx_r=x_{r+1}\phi_r$, $\phi_rx_{r+1}=x_r\phi_r$ and $\phi_r^2=1-\delta^2$. On a generalized joint weight whose adjacent entries differ by neither $1$ nor $-1$, $1-\delta^2$ is invertible by a finite nilpotent geometric series; hence the swapped weight is nonzero. If any entry of a nonzero weight is not integral, move its leftmost nonintegral entry left across all preceding integral entries. The swaps are invertible, but the resulting first entry contradicts $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$. Thus all spectra are integral. For each position separately choose an annihilator $p_r(z)=\prod_{a\in S_r}(z-a)^{N_r}$ from its finite regular spectrum, with $N_r=\dim H_d(m)$ sufficient. Chinese remainder interpolation gives mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors $E_{r,a}(x_r)$ summing to one. Their products $e(i)=\prod_r E_{r,i_r}(x_r)$ give exactly the simultaneous generalized-weight projectors on every finite module; algebra identities follow from regular faithfulness. There is no assertion that the first-position cyclotomic polynomial annihilates other dots. [F5, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 **The content-block centre comparison.** In an admissible stable realization the actual endomorphism theorem identifies $H:=H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$. Choose a projective generator $Q$ of the genuine block containing $T_\alpha$, and put $A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$ and $M=\pi Q$. Full faithfulness on projectives identifies $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)$ with $\operatorname{End}_H(M)$, and $M$ contains the regular left module $\pi T_\alpha=H$. No projectivity of all of $M$ over $H$ is assumed. [given, construct, algebra]

1.3 **The exact centre calculation.** A central endomorphism $z$ of $M$ restricts on $H$ to right multiplication $R_h$. Commuting with every $R_b$ forces $h\in Z(H)$. For each $m\in M$, the map $f_m:H\to M$, $a\mapsto am$, commutes with $z$; evaluation at one gives $z(m)=hm$. Conversely multiplication by central $h$ commutes with every $H$-map. These constructions are inverse, proving $Z(\operatorname{End}_H M)=Z(H)$, and passage to opposite rings preserves centres. The stated Choice assumption is inherited only for the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Central content interpolation.** Symmetric polynomials in the dots commute with crossings by the native cross relations, because $s_r$ commutes with $x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $x_rx_{r+1}$ and with all other dots; these generate the elementary symmetric polynomials. Their elementary symmetric values distinguish the finitely many different multisets of generalized joint eigenvalues. Finite Chinese remainder interpolation in these symmetric operators therefore gives a central multiset projector. Its action on every regular generalized weight is one precisely on that multiset, so it equals the orbit sum $e_\alpha$ of the per-position projectors from step 1.1. This argument does not require the annihilating polynomials for different positions to be equal. [F5, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 **A single linkage block has no split central idempotent.** $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a single linkage block by [[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]: it admits no decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal factors. A central idempotent $f=f^2\ne0$ of $A$ with $f\ne1$ would split the projective generator $Q=Qf\oplus Q(1-f)$ into two nonzero summands whose Hom-spaces in both directions vanish, because every morphism between them is annihilated by composing with $f$ on either side in the two possible orders; this exhibits $\mathcal O_\alpha$ as the product of the two nonzero full subcategories generated by these summands, contradicting single-linkage. Hence $Z(A)$ has no nontrivial idempotent, and by step 1.2 the same holds for $Z(H)=Z(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$: the stable content component is a single block. [step 1.2, step 1.3, given, algebra]

3.1 **Symmetric polynomials in the $x_r$ are central.** It suffices to show that the elementary symmetric functions in the $x_r$ are fixed by conjugation with each basic transposition $s_r$, since these generate the symmetric polynomials and commute with all $x_i$ with $i\notin\{r,r+1\}$. The defining cross relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ and $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$; multiplying the first by $s_r$ on the left yields $s_rx_{r+1}s_r=x_r+s_r$, and the second yields $s_rx_rs_r=x_{r+1}-s_r$. Consequently $s_r(x_r+x_{r+1})s_r=x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $s_r(x_rx_{r+1})s_r=(x_{r+1}-s_r)(x_r+s_r)=x_rx_{r+1}$, so the two elementary generators in the pair $\{x_r,x_{r+1}\}$ are fixed, and $s_r^2=1$ makes the same true for every polynomial in them; together with the commuting generators this fixes every symmetric polynomial. Comparing with step 2.1, $e_\alpha$ commutes with every $x_i$ and every $s_r$, hence is central in $H_d(m)$. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 **Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set and fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations to be performed. Choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and an upper endpoint $r$ so that every charge $m_j$ lies in the letter alphabet $[k,r+1]$ and every simple-root support occurring in the list lies in $[k,r]$; enlarge an auxiliary stable realization only in the direction of the stable range, so that the added bottom rows of every tableau are forced to keep the ground entry in every column and every added top entry is absent. By the actual double-cut/common-tail compatibility and the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] and [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], the $I$-supported content component $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the same finite-dimensional algebra as the corresponding content component of the stable realization, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, the same residue projectors and the same residue maps; no whole-degree equality is used. Applying step 2.2 to that common component proves (b) for arbitrary consecutive $I$. [step 2.2, given, algebra]

4.1 **Nonzeroness is open.** Centrality neither makes $e_\alpha$ primitive nor excludes $e_\alpha=0$; both questions are settled by steps 2.2 and 3.2 using the stable realization, whose hypotheses are the ones declared in the Given. [step 3.1, given]

5.1 **Level zero and the vanishing witness.** At level $0$ the cyclotomic polynomial is the empty product $1$, so $H_d(m)=0$ for $d>0$ and only $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ remains; this is the convention of (2). For the witness, $I=\{0\}$, level $1$, charge $(0)$, $d=2$: the level-one presentation gives $x_1=0$ and $x_2=s_1$, so $H_2(0)=\mathbb C[S_2]$ with eigenvalues $\pm1$ for $x_2$; hence $E_0(x_2)=0$, $e(0,0)=0$, and the supported component $H^\Lambda_{2\alpha_0}=e_{(0,0)}H_2(0)$ is $0$, while $H_2(0)\ne0$. This completes the proof of the two claims (b) and the level-$0$ convention; the exactness and biadjointness clauses of (4) are the declared supplier statements of [[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]], not reproved here. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke $G_0$ is the dual highest weight module
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting of the tower: $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ is nonempty,
consecutive and bounded below, $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ is an admitted integral
multicharge, and $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]. Let
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ be the column-strict, respectively
standard, tableaux of the Fock data of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]], with monomials $M_A$ and
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$, canonical vectors $T_A$ and quasi-canonical vectors
$P_A$ as in [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and
let $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ be the normalized highest projection, so that
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and $S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$. Work at source
parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The exact Schur quotient identifies the module Grothendieck group
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the FULL integral costandard lattice
$$V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\,D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A\ :\ A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\,\}$$
by $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, and it sends every Specht class to
$[S(B)]\mapsto S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$; the vectors
$\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ are another integral basis, the standard
monomial basis.

**(ii)** The endomorphisms of $G_0$ induced by the residue functors $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of the integrable
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock action, and both the standard and the costandard
integral forms carry the actual divided-power action.

**(iii)** Over $\mathbb Q$ the ground class generates the dual highest weight
module $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$. Over $\mathbb Z$ the costandard lattice need
NOT be ground cyclic, even under divided powers: the rank-one case
$I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$ has a ground-generated integral lattice of
index two that omits $D_{01}$. The STANDARD lattice, by contrast, is integrally
generated by its ground vector under divided powers.

**(iv)** Every standard-tableau simple occurs as a composition factor of a
residue word applied to the ground simple, and the ground crystal component is
exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$.

**(v)** The categorical reachability and rational-cyclicity statements of
(iii)-(iv) do not imply integral costandard cyclicity; the level-$0$ tower has
only the ground weight.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The bounded-below tower $H^\Lambda$ of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the Fock data
and its four families as in
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], the exact
Schur quotient $\pi$ with its left adjoint $\pi^*$ as in
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and
[[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], and the assumption of the
Axiom of Choice used by the imported suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). We prove (i)-(v).

[F1] Every object of the category of finite-dimensional modules over a
finite-dimensional algebra has finite length, so the classes of simples form a
$\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0$, with composition multiplicities as coordinates
([[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]]).

[F2] A class function on isomorphism classes that is additive on short exact
sequences factors uniquely through $G_0$, and an exact functor induces a
homomorphism of $G_0$ functorially
([[thm-grothendieck-group-universal-properties-and-functoriality]]).

[F3] The Axiom of Choice holds: every family of nonempty sets has a choice
function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $L(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]]. [F1, F3, given, construct]

1.2 **The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]. [given, construct]

1.3 **The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]. [given, construct]

2.1 **The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, construct]

2.2 **The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a Jordan–Hölder composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):L(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):L(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, F2, algebra]

2.3 **Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is generated by the ground vector $D_{A_\Lambda}$ over $\mathbb Q$ and is identified with the form-dual family by the same theorem. The ground-generation use is the actual definition $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], specialized at one; it concerns the standard lattice only. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 **Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2]. The natural intertwining isomorphisms $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$ of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]], together with the category-O Chevalley action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], show that $[\pi]$ is a module map. Steps 1.1–2.2 identify its kernel with the span of the off-standard simple classes, precisely the kernel of the Fock projection. Thus the induced quotient map $\Phi$ intertwines $e_i,f_i$, proving the ordinary Chevalley clause of (ii). No head, socle or indecomposability assertion is inferred merely from exactness of a quotient. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F2, given, algebra]

3.2 **Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with both lattices equal to the ground line and every residue operator zero. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v). [step 1.1, step 2.1, given]

4.1 **Crystal reachability and composition factors.** The source upper ground component is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space, so over $\mathbb Q$ it identifies the full costandard lattice's scalar extension with the irreducible highest module. Its highest vector therefore generates that module under lowering divided powers. Consequently every basis vector $D_A$ is a rational linear combination of lowering words applied to the ground vector. By step 3.1 each ordinary lowering word is the class of the corresponding exact residue-word module, with nonnegative simple-class coefficients by [F1]. If $D(A)$ occurred in none of these modules, every such word and every rational linear combination would have zero $D_A$ coefficient, contrary to the coefficient one in $D_A$. Thus some residue word contains $D(A)$ as a composition factor. This proves (iv) without requiring integral costandard generation or transport of head and socle through the quotient. [step 2.1, step 2.3, step 3.1, F1, given, algebra]

5.1 **Rational ground cyclicity.** The normalized $E/F$-contravariant highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space. Thus its weightwise duality identifies $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, interpreted as the direct sum of the costandard weight spaces, with the irreducible rational highest module. The ground vector maps to the normalized highest vector; its orbit under lowering divided powers therefore spans every weight space, as used in step 4.1. This proves the rational clause of (iii). The full unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module is not used. [step 2.3, step 3.1, step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 **The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. The supported degree-one block is $B_0=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ and the supported degree-two block is $M_2(\mathbb C)$, with its simple represented by $x_1=N=E_{12}$, $s_1=-(E_{12}+E_{21})$ and $x_2=-N$. The first dot is not zero on that simple. The actual residue Ind/Res dimensions give $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$ and $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$, with the end actions zero. Their divided squares give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. Therefore $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$ and all their divided powers, contains the ground vector and excludes $D_{01}$. This is a proper integral costandard submodule, whereas over $\mathbb Q$ division by two recovers $D_{01}$. Degree one is not called a corner sitting inside degree two. [step 2.3, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Conclusion.** Step 2.1 identifies $G_0$ with the full integral costandard lattice and step 2.2 computes the Specht classes, proving (i); step 2.3 gives the divided-power integral forms and step 3.1 identifies the residue operators with the Chevalley operators, proving (ii); step 5.1 proves rational ground cyclicity, step 2.3 proves integral ground generation of the standard lattice and step 6.1 exhibits the index-two failure of integral costandard cyclicity, proving (iii) and its sharpness; step 4.1 proves the crystal reachability statement (iv); and step 3.2 (level zero) together with steps 5.1 and 6.1 separates the rational-cyclicity and categorical reachability conclusions from integral costandard cyclicity, as asserted in (v). No step identifies $\{D_A\}$ with the standard divided-power lattice, and no integral costandard generation is used. [step 2.2, step 2.3, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 3.2, given] ∎

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke projective $K_0$ is the highest weight module
items.statement:
Assume inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the category-O, Fock/global and quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting, the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], and the Fock data
with the four bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].
For $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ let $D(A)$ be the simple module of the
identification of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and let $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ be its projective cover in
$\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$. Work at source parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The assignment $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ is an isomorphism from the split
Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ of finite-dimensional
projective modules onto the standard highest weight lattice
$V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$,
so $\{P_A\}$ is a $\mathbb Z$-basis; at parameter one the source vector $P_A$
coincides with $T_{A^\uparrow}$, and the lattice is integrally generated by its
ground vector under divided powers.

**(ii)** Under the identifications (i) and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
the map $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\to G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ induced
by the embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules is the
natural injective inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$
of the standard lattice into the full costandard lattice.

**(iii)** The Cartan Hom pairing becomes the normalized highest pairing: with
the projected simple vectors $D_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B$ one has
$C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; these are projected simple vectors, not an
unqualified identification of monomials with simples.

**(iv)** Both residue functors $e_i$ and $f_i$ on projective modules induce
operators on $K_0$ that are the Chevalley operators adjoint to their $G_0$
operators of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]].

**(v)** The left adjoint $\pi^*$ of the Schur quotient is right exact on all
modules, sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives and recovers the
standard-labelled prinjectives; exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules is
neither asserted nor needed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inherited Axiom of Choice and the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its block-wise Grothendieck groups as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the exact Schur
quotient $\pi$ with right-exact left adjoint $\pi^*$ of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], the
Schur-image identifications $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$, $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$,
$\pi(P(A))=Y(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and
$\pi^*\pi(P(A))=P(A)$ of
[[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]],
and the Fock dictionary $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}(P_A)=P_A$, $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$
at parameter one. We prove (i)-(v).

[F1] Finite-dimensional projective modules over a finite-dimensional algebra
have a free split Grothendieck group on the classes of the projective covers
([[thm-finite-dimensional-algebra-projective-classes-form-a-split-k-zero-basis]]).

[F2] On object pairs the Cartan pairing is
$\langle[P],[M]\rangle=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)$, its descent to
$K_0\times G_0$ and the duality of the two bases are proved in
[[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]] (definition:
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]).

[F3] Exact adjoint functors acting compatibly on projectives induce adjoint maps
of Grothendieck groups for the Hom pairing
([[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The split $K_0$ basis of covers.** Every simple finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-module has a projective cover, unique up to isomorphism, and the classes $[Y(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, of the covers of the simples $D(A)$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the split Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules; this is [F1] applied block by block and summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. [F1, given, construct]

1.2 **The left adjoint on projectives.** The Schur quotient $\pi$ has a left adjoint $\pi^*$ which is right exact on all modules and sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $\pi^*(Y(A))=P(A)$ and $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so $\pi^*$ recovers the standard-labelled prinjectives, and its exactness on arbitrary modules is not needed. These are the statements of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]. [given, construct]

1.3 **The standard lattice and its ground generation.** The standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ has $\mathbb Z$-basis $\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$, the source vector $P_A$ lies in the highest constituent with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}P_A=P_A$, and at parameter one $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}=G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)$, so $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ is integrally generated by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators: the actual lower lattice is $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. This is the parameter-one specialization of [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the basis statements of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]. [given, algebra]

2.1 **The identification $K_0\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$.** Define $\Psi$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Psi([Y(A)])=P_A$; by step 1.3 both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules on the same index set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, so $\Psi$ is a group isomorphism onto $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, giving (i). The identification is realized functorially by $\pi^*$: step 1.2 shows that on projective classes the composite of $\pi^*$ with the category-O identification $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ at parameter one (the projective half of the tableau $K_0$/Fock identification of [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], proved in [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]) is $\Psi$, so no exactness of $\pi^*$ on non-projectives is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given, construct]

3.1 **The inclusion is the lattice inclusion.** The embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules induces a map on Grothendieck groups; in the category of finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-modules a projective class $[Y(A)]$ maps to the class of the same module, which under the identification $\Phi$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] is the costandard coordinate vector of the module $Y(A)$. By step 1.2, $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so this vector equals the image of $[P(A)]$ under the exact quotient, namely $P_A$ by step 1.3. Hence the composite $\Phi\circ(\text{inclusion})\circ\Psi^{-1}$ is the identity on the basis $\{P_A\}$, i.e. the natural inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$. It is injective because the vectors $P_A$ are linearly independent in the rational highest module, and hence also as elements of its full costandard lattice. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space; no claim that the embedded standard and costandard lattices coincide is used. This proves (ii). [step 1.3, step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 **The Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing.** By [F2] the Cartan pairing descends to $K_0\times G_0$ and pairs the two bases dually; under the identifications of step 2.1 and of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the value on basis vectors is computed on the Fock side, where the pairing between the standard and costandard families at parameter one is the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ with $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ by [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. This proves (iii); in particular the costandard vectors entering the pairing are the projected simples $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$, not unprojected monomials. [step 2.1, F2, given, algebra]

4.1 **Chevalley operators on $K_0$.** Use the actual exact residue biadjunction from the tower supplier. For projective $P$ over the source, $\operatorname{Hom}(f_iP,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_i-)$ is exact, so $f_iP$ is projective; for projective $Q$ over the target, $\operatorname{Hom}(e_iQ,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(Q,f_i-)$ is exact, so $e_iQ$ is projective. Applying an idempotent by itself would not prove projectivity over a different algebra. These functors induce the adjoint operators of [F3] under the Hom pairing. Their $G_0$ counterparts are the already identified Chevalley operators, and the normalized highest pairing makes $e_i,f_i$ adjoint, so the same identification holds on $K_0$. [step 1.2, step 3.2, F3, given, algebra]

5.1 **Conclusion.** Step 2.1 proves (i), step 3.1 proves the lattice-inclusion statement (ii), step 3.2 proves the pairing statement (iii) with its projected-simple qualification, step 4.1 proves (iv), and the properties of the right-exact left adjoint stated in step 1.2 are exactly the assertion (v); at no point is exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules, or a recovery of all category-O projectives, assumed. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, given] ∎

items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$
(equivalently $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$);

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of
$\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$;

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
$D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$);

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being the rectification
$A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ and its inverse $\downarrow$ between
$\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks,
intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible
finite pieces give the original arbitrary-$I$ statement. At level $0$ only
$\alpha=0$ and the ground survive.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The bounded-below data and the tower $H^\Lambda$ of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the two
identifications of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]],
the Fock data of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] with its four
families of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
the category-O side of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
as well as the Axiom of Choice as used by the imported suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). We prove (i)-(iv) and the arbitrary-$I$ extension.

[F1] The classes of simples form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0$ for a
finite-dimensional algebra, with composition multiplicities as coordinates
([[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]]).

[F2] The Axiom of Choice holds: every family of nonempty sets has a choice
function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Both identifications and their duality.** By [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the map $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$ identifies $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and is compatible with the standard classes $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$; by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]] the map $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ identifies $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ with the standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, the embedding of projectives induces the lattice inclusion, and the Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. Since the two lattice identifications are the actual source dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]] at parameter one, the identifications hold simultaneously and are mutually dual. [F2, given, algebra]

1.2 **The residue rule for simples: required local input.** The intertwining of residue functors and their dualities, together with the Schur-image classification, identifies $e_i^HD(A)$ with $\pi(e_i^OL(A))$ and similarly for $f_i$. To conclude (iii), one must additionally prove on these actual translated objects that the quotient preserves the unique surviving head and socle and yields a nonzero indecomposable exactly along the corresponding standard crystal edge. Exactness of a Serre quotient alone does not establish these properties. This is a held prerequisite of this draft: the current local Schur/translation carriers and their reflected-left Whittaker input have not supplied an accepted proof of that transfer. Clause (iii), and every later reference to its proof in this paragraph, remains pending; no full-faithfulness or generator assertion is inferred here. [F2, given]

1.3 **The parameter-one normalization and label bijections.** At parameter one the quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ and the costandard family is $D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ with $A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ the rectification from reverse-standard to standard tableaux and $\downarrow$ its inverse, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] and [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]; this gives (iv). [F2, given, algebra]

1.4 **Level zero.** For level $0$ the tower has $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$ by the level-zero convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], so only $\alpha=0$ and the ground class remain, consistently with the two identifications being the rank-one lattices $\mathbb ZP_\varnothing=\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$. [given]

2.1 **The decomposition formula (i).** The formula $[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is the standard-class half of the identification of step 1.1; the coefficient dictionary $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$, $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$ is that of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and the full polynomial transition matrix, its unitriangularity and the restriction to standard simple labels are those of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. This proves (i); no off-standard label is made a simple class. [step 1.1, F1, given, algebra]

2.2 **The Chevalley operators (ii).** The residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]], and the corresponding statement on $K_0$ for projective classes is [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]; on the category-O side both statements are the integrable Fock action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] transferred by the exact Schur quotient of step 1.2. This proves (ii). [step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

2.3 **Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set (possibly unbounded above or below), fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations, and choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and upper endpoint $r$ so that the LETTER alphabet $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and the ROOT interval $[k,r]$ contains the support of $\alpha$ and every shifted support occurring in the operations. The common-tail and double-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], shows that added bottom occupancy is maximal in every column (so every new entry is forced ground) and added top occupancy is zero, and that the monomial, bar, global and projected basis equations are unchanged on the selected finite weight set. Hence the Hecke block is the same content component of the same $H_d(m)$, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, projective and simple labels, residue projectors and residue maps, and the blockwise statements of (i)-(iv) glue along these compatible finite pieces to give the arbitrary-$I$ statement. At the level of the block decomposition of the tower, the excluded blocks for $I\ne\mathbb Z$ are real (the supported cut is proper by [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]), and no equality of $H^\Lambda$ with $\bigoplus_dH_d(m)$ is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given, algebra]

3.1 **Dependency of the conclusion.** Step 1.1 and steps 2.1–2.2 assemble the simultaneous dual identifications, decomposition formula and Chevalley action conditional on the two Grothendieck suppliers; step 1.3 records the parameter-one normalization and label bijections, step 2.3 the arbitrary-consecutive-$I$ extension conditional on the stated cut and same-block contracts, and step 1.4 the level-zero case. Completion of (iii) still requires the held local prerequisite identified in step 1.2. Thus the entire original Statement is retained as the target of this draft, while this recovery does not claim a completed proof or mathematical acceptance of the whole theorem. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, given] ∎

items.title: The degenerate and nondegenerate Ariki theorems have distinct parameter ranges
items.statement:
The degenerate theorem [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]] concerns
the tower over $\mathbb C$ with integral multicharge
$m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, additive cyclotomic roots $m_j$, and the
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock/highest-weight data. Its Grothendieck-group,
projective/simple, standard-class and decomposition-number identifications
are ungraded at the basis parameter one. That parameter is independent of
the nondegenerate numerical Hecke parameter $\xi$.

There are two distinct nondegenerate comparisons. In the generic branch,
$\xi\in\mathbb C^\times$ has infinite multiplicative order,
$Q_j=\xi^{m_j}$, residues are integers and the quiver is type $A_\infty$
(quantum characteristic $e=0$). The characteristic-zero generic theorem is
equivalent to the degenerate theorem through the coherent comparison of
towers and standard classes described below. At a primitive $e$-th root of
unity $\xi\ne1$, residues are modulo $e$ and the datum is cyclic affine type
$A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, including the double edge at $e=2$. The latter theorem needs
its own comparison and categorification results; it does not follow by
specializing the generic algebra isomorphism.
items.strategy: The remark separates conventions rather than proving a new claim. (1) The degenerate statement is exactly the content of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]] with its integral charge and parameter-one Fock data. (2) The generic isomorphism is Corollary 2 of the cyclotomic Hecke/KLR paper: over a characteristic-zero field, $H^\Lambda_d$ for $q$ not a root of unity is isomorphic to $H^\Lambda_d$ for $q=1$; the same source notes that Ariki's theorem for generic $q$ is thereby equivalent to the degenerate theorem, which is precisely the limitation of the bridge. (3) At a root of unity the source's Main Theorem replaces the rational degeneration by the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR algebra of type $A_\infty$ (for $e=0$) or $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$ (for $e>0$), and the accompanying grading is an extra structure not present in the degenerate data; the graded decomposition-number theorems are therefore separate results (the QG-8 route of this run). (4) The level-one instance records the difference concretely: the degenerate tower is $H^{(m)}_d=\mathbb C[S_d]$, whereas the nondegenerate Hecke algebra is a deformation with its own parameter dependence and semisimplicity behaviour; the two must be recorded with their own parameters and no implication between the theorems is asserted. Keep the genuine original full-reading/source provenance for this comparison. No optional local Hecke–KLR proof reconstruction or future empty QG8 prerequisite is claimed. Use the explicit generic normalization above, and use the corrected supported tower when referring to a finite residue interval.

items.title: Degenerate Specht decomposition numbers are canonical basis coefficients at one
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Use the actual source chart at parameter $s$: with the monomials $M_A$ and the
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$ of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], put

$$R_{A,B}(s)=p_{A,B}(-s),\qquad L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A,\qquad M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A . $$

Thus $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ is the INVERSE of $R(s)$, not its transpose. Also
$P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$.

**(i)** For every Specht label $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ and every simple label
$A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $[S(B):D(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$.

**(ii)** In the usual Specht-row/simple-column notation the rectangular
decomposition matrix is the transpose of $D$ restricted to standard rows; it is
NOT the transpose of the $L$-in-$M$ chart. The full matrix $D$ is unitriangular
on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, and its square submatrix on standard columns is
unitriangular; in particular $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ only for
$B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, since for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the object
$D(B)=0$ is not a simple module label.

**(iii)** Retain the type-$A$ polynomial formula: for the right place action,
$w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the ENTRY stabilizer $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, and

$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}),$$

while the COLUMN Levi $J$ is a distinct group; the mixed singular/parabolic
composition matrix is the finite Levi cancellation sum over $C$ column-equivalent
to $B$, $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$, and equals
$d_{A,B}(1)$. All categorification multiplicities are ungraded at parameter
one, with the source/library reciprocal convention.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The inherited Axiom of Choice and the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors, the two
identifications of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]], and the coefficient dictionary
of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]. We prove
(i)-(iii).

[F1] The classes of simples of a finite-dimensional algebra form a
$\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0$, with coordinates the composition multiplicities
([[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]]).

[F2] The Schur quotient realizes the identification of
[[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]: the simple classes are indexed by
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and the Specht classes satisfy $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, with
the quotient exact on the standard quotient of the block.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The two charts are mutually inverse.** By [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] the vectors $L_B$ and $M_A$ are two $\mathbb Z[s,s^{-1}]$-bases of the finite weight spaces of the Fock module, so the transition matrices $R(s)=(p_{A,B}(-s))$ with $L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A$ and $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ with $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$ satisfy $R(s)D(s)=D(s)R(s)=1$; both are triangular with diagonal entries $1$ on each weight block, and the quasi-canonical vector is $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$. The polynomial entries and the chart conventions are those of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]. [given, algebra]

1.2 **The type-$A$ polynomial dictionary.** The explicit transition coefficients are given by the type-$A$ formulas of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]: for the right place action, $w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the entry stabilizer $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, $p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2})$, the column Levi $J$ is distinct from $K$, and the mixed singular/parabolic composition coefficient is the finite Levi cancellation sum $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$. [given, construct]

2.1 **The O-side multiplicity dictionary.** On the category-O side the standard module $N(B)$ has a composition series whose multiplicities with respect to the simples $L(A)$ are read off in the same chart: the coefficient of $M_B$ in the expansion of $P_A$ is the multiplicity of $L(A)$ in $N(B)$ at parameter one, in the source's reciprocal convention, by [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; combined with step 1.1 this gives $[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for all $A,B$, with $d_{A,B}$ unitriangular, and $[N(B):L(B)]=1$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ in the full square matrix. [step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 **Transfer to the Hecke side.** By [F2] the Schur quotient is exact, sends $N(B)$ to $S(B)$, $L(A)$ to $D(A)$ for standard $A$ and kills the off-standard simples; applying it to a composition series of $N(B)$ and using [F1] gives $[S(B):D(A)]=[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, the sum being finite on each weight block. This proves (i). [F2, step 2.1, F1, given]

4.1 **Shape of the matrix.** The full matrix $D=(d_{A,B})$ is unitriangular on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1; restricting rows to the simple labels $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ (all of which occur, and which index the simples by [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]) leaves a rectangular matrix, whose square submatrix on the standard columns is again unitriangular with diagonal entries $1$. Off standard columns the equation $D(B)=0$ says precisely that $D(B)$ is not a simple module label, so the identity $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ is asserted only for $B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. This proves (ii). The statement is not that the rectangular matrix is invertible, and no off-standard simple is created. [step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 **The polynomial coefficient is not a transposed inverse.** The decomposition matrix of (i) has rows the simple labels and columns the Specht labels, and its entries are the coefficients of $D(s)$ at $s=1$; since $R(s)=D(s)^{-1}$, its transpose is $D(s)^{-t}$, which is in general different from the $L$-in-$M$ chart $R(s)$. On the two-factor space with labels $01<10$ one has $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, so $R_{01,10}=-s$ is the negative-entry chart, whereas its inverse has $D_{01,10}=s$, while the true decomposition entry is $d_{01,10}(1)=1$: $S(10)$ is the simple $D(01)$ and not a formal negative combination. Hence with simple rows and Specht columns the decomposition matrix is the standard-row restriction of $D$; with Specht rows and simple columns it is its transpose. Neither convention uses the transpose of $R$. This completes (iii) together with steps 1.2, whose entry stabilizer $K$ and column Levi $J$ remain distinct and whose multiplicities are the finite Levi cancellation values at parameter one; all statements are ungraded. [step 3.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: Projective and simple dual bases in a degenerate cyclotomic block
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the categorification and based-module identifications; the explicit finite calculations below are choice-free.

For $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, the degree-one supported block
$B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]])
has simple $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ with $x\mapsto0$ and projective cover $Y_{01}=B$.
Therefore $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$ in $G_0$, whereas
$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{01},D_{01})=1$. At parameter one the categorification
images of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]] and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]
are

$$P_{00}=D_{00}=M_{00},\qquad P_{01}=M_{01}+M_{10},\qquad D_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10}),\qquad P_{11}=D_{11}=M_{11}.$$

The simple image is the PROJECTED vector $\pi L_{01}$, not the unprojected
$L_{01}=M_{01}$. With the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ one has
$C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ across these three weights. In the degree-two block
$M_2(\mathbb C)$, the simple $D_{11}$ is two-dimensional and is itself its
projective cover; the abstract Fock weight is one-dimensional, not the
underlying module. Thus the composition Cartan values are $1,2,1$, while the
projective/simple Hom pairing is the identity. Projective covers are self-dual
here by the actual symmetric block forms, not merely because their heads are
self-dual.

In the costandard basis $(D_{00},D_{01},D_{11})$,

$$fD_{00}=2D_{01},\quad fD_{01}=D_{11},\quad fD_{11}=0;\qquad eD_{00}=0,\quad eD_{01}=D_{00},\quad eD_{11}=2D_{01}.$$

The divided powers give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$, with
all other second divided moves $0$. Hence the integral ground-generated lattice
is EXACTLY $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$, of index
$2$ in the full costandard lattice
$\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$. The standard lattice
has basis $(P_{00},P_{01},P_{11})$, is integrally divided-power generated by its
ground, and pairs perfectly with the full costandard lattice. Costandard ground
cyclicity holds over $\mathbb Q$, not over $\mathbb Z$; crystal and
composition-factor reachability do not imply integral vector generation.

cover and simple bases dually
([[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]],
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The degree-one block.** For $I=\{0\}$, level $2$ and charge $(0,0)$ the degree-one cyclotomic quotient is $H^{(0,0)}_1=\mathbb C[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ by the level-two instance of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], and it is already supported, so $B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ with $x=x_1$. Its radical is $(x)$ and its quotient is $\mathbb C$, so $B$ is local; the unique simple is $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ with $x\mapsto0$, the regular module $Y_{01}=B$ is its projective cover, and the regular composition series $0\subset(x)\subset B$ has successive quotients $D_{01},D_{01}$, giving $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$ in $G_0$. Every $B$-linear map $B\to D_{01}$ is determined by the image of $1$, so $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{01},D_{01})=1$. [given, algebra]

2.1 **The symmetric form on $B$ and self-duality.** The coefficient functional $\tau(a+bx)=b$ is a symmetrizing trace on $B$: it is linear, $\tau(uv)=\tau(vu)$ for all $u,v$ (both sides pick out the $x$-coefficient of the product), and its radical is zero because $\tau(x)\ne0$, so the associated form $\langle u,v\rangle=\tau(uv)$ has matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ in the basis $(1,x)$, which is nonsingular. The anti-involution $\ast$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] that fixes $x$ is the identity of $B$ here, so the form is generator-fixing, and it exhibits an isomorphism $Y_{01}\cong Y_{01}^{\circledast}$: the dual of the regular module with respect to the trace. This is the actual symmetric-algebra proof of cover self-duality, not an inference from self-duality of the head. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 **The degree-two block and its simple.** With $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$ the relations give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$, $x^2=0$, and from $ux^2=0$ one gets $y^2=(x+y)u$, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-two algebra; the models $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ and $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ satisfy all relations, and $z=x+y$ is central with images $0,1+2\epsilon,-1+2\epsilon$; the Hermite polynomials $E_0=(1-z^2)^2$, $E_\pm=(1-E_0\pm(3z-z^3)/2)/2$ map to the separate factor identities. Each factor is generated by its images of $x,u$, so the homomorphism is onto the eight-dimensional product; the eight-word spanning bound proves that the span of the eight words is isomorphic to $M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$. The supported content cut at $2\alpha_0$ keeps the factor $M_2(\mathbb C)$; its simple module $\mathbb C^2$ has Gram matrix $J$, since $N^{t}J=JN$ and $(-J)^{t}J=J(-J)$, and it is self-dual and projective, so its projective cover is itself and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$; degree $0$ contributes $\mathbb C$, and Hom-spaces between distinct content blocks vanish because they are different blocks. In particular the one-dimensional Fock weight vector $M_{11}$ is not the two-dimensional module $D_{11}$, and the degree-two projective cover has vector-space dimension $2$ and composition length $1$. Higher supported degrees vanish directly: in an all-zero-residue module on at least three strands, restriction to strands $1,2$ forces $x_2=-x_1$ and $x_1^2=0$ by the matrix factor. Since $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$, it commutes with $x_2$, and the recursion gives $x_3=x_2+s_2$. On either $s_2$ eigenspace this is $x_2\pm1$, which is invertible, contradicting nilpotence of $x_3$ at residue zero. Thus such a nonzero module cannot exist; applying this to the regular module proves the supported algebra is zero in every degree at least three. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 **The projected dual bases at parameter one.** In the tensor square at parameter one, $fM_{00}=M_{01}+M_{10}$, $f(M_{01}+M_{10})=2M_{11}$, and $e$ reverses these moves with coefficients $2,1$. Hence the ground constituent has basis $P_{00},P_{01},P_{11}$ as displayed, and its complementary trivial line is $M_{10}-M_{01}$. Projection along this line gives $D_{01}=\pi M_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$ and fixes the endpoints. The normalized form is determined by $C_0(M_{00},M_{00})=1$, $e/f$ adjunction and orthogonality of distinct weights: $C_0(P_{01},P_{01})=C_0(M_{00},eP_{01})=2$, and $2C_0(P_{11},P_{11})=C_0(P_{01},eP_{11})=2$. Thus the mixed vector is $P_{01}=M_{01}+M_{10}$ of $C_0$-norm $2$, so the correct field dual is $D_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$, and the endpoint vectors satisfy $P_{00}=D_{00}=M_{00}$ and $P_{11}=D_{11}=M_{11}$. The Gram matrix in the $D$-basis is $\operatorname{diag}(1,\tfrac12,1)$, and multiplying its first-argument basis by $\operatorname{diag}(1,2,1)$ gives the identity matrix, which is the pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; this directly computes the parameter-one projected-simple dictionary of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]], not an identification of $L_{01}=M_{01}$ with the simple. [step 2.2, given, algebra]

4.1 **The categorified residue operators.** In these all-zero-residue blocks the residue projectors are the identities, so the bimodules are the explicit tower-inclusion bimodules. Induction from degree $0$ to the degree-one block gives the regular module of $B$; the supported induction from $B$ to the degree-two block $M_2(\mathbb C)$ sends the simple $\mathbb C$ to $\mathbb C^2$ and the regular module $B$ to $M_2(\mathbb C)$, which is two copies of the simple $\mathbb C^2$; explicitly $M_2\otimes_B\mathbb C=M_2/M_2N$ has dimension two and is the unique matrix-factor simple, whereas $M_2\otimes_B B=M_2$; restriction of $\mathbb C^2$ to $B$ is the regular Jordan module $B$ itself (the generator $x$ of $B$ acts on $\mathbb C^2$ as $N$ with $N^2=0$ and $\dim\ker N=1$), and restriction of $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ to degree zero is the one-dimensional $\mathbb C$-module. The right $B$-module $M_2$ is free of rank two: each row is a regular $B$-module for right multiplication by $N$, so these induction functors are exact directly. These explicit bimodules realize the residue functors of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]] and yield the displayed columns $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$, $fD_{11}=0$ and $eD_{00}=0$, $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$; equivalently, in the $D$-basis, $f$ has columns $(0,2,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,0,1)^{\mathsf T},0$ and $e$ has columns $0,(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,2,0)^{\mathsf T}$, so $[e,f]=ef-fe$ is $\operatorname{diag}(2,0,-2)$ in the $sl_2$-normalization of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]. [step 2.2, step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 **The normalized finite identifications.** On projective classes the same bimodules give $f[Y_{00}]=[Y_{01}]$, $f[Y_{01}]=2[Y_{11}]$, $e[Y_{01}]=2[Y_{00}]$ and $e[Y_{11}]=[Y_{01}]$. On simple classes they give step 4.1. Therefore the maps $[Y_A]\mapsto P_A$ and $[D_A]\mapsto D_A$ intertwine both $e$ and $f$ with the explicit Fock matrices of step 3.1 and send the degree-zero class to the normalized ground. Over $\mathbb Q$ each module is ground generated, so these normalized intertwining maps are unique; consequently they agree with any named categorification identification with that normalization, rather than assuming a general bridge to establish this finite instance. Each cover/simple Hom space within a block has dimension one, by step 1.1 and the scalar endomorphism ring in step 2.2, while different degrees give zero Hom in the tower direct sum. Exactness of Hom from a projective makes the pairing additive on short exact sequences, so the pairing matrix is the identity on these bases. Its vector realization is precisely $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ from step 3.1, and the composition Cartan matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(1,2,1)$. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 **The index-two lattice and its cyclicity.** The divided powers $f^{(2)}=f^2/2$ and $e^{(2)}=e^2/2$ give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$, and the displayed matrices preserve evenness of the $D_{01}$-coordinate whenever the input has that coordinate even, so the lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$, their divided powers and the toral operators at weights $2,0,-2$. It is generated from the ground because $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$ and $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$. Its elements have $D_{01}$-coordinate even, so it does not contain $D_{01}$; hence it is a proper integral submodule containing the ground, of index $2$ in the full costandard lattice, and $D_{01}$ is not in the integral ground-generated span. Over $\mathbb Q$ division by $2$ is available, so the ground vector generates the whole three-dimensional costandard space; the standard lattice is by step 5.1 the lattice with basis $(P_{00},P_{01},P_{11})$, which is integrally generated by its ground under the divided powers and pairs perfectly with the full costandard lattice by step 3.1. This proves that integral costandard generation fails while the full integral duality and the standard divided-power statement survive. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, given, algebra]

7.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 verify the degree-one cover, its composition length against its Hom dimension, and the symmetric-form self-duality; step 2.2 and step 3.1 verify the degree-two block, the projected dual bases and the pairing identity; step 4.1 verifies the residue operators, their commutator and the categorified $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$; step 6.1 verifies the exact index-two lattice, its stability, its failure to contain $D_{01}$ and the rational cyclicity. No step identifies the simple image with the unprojected monomial $L_{01}$, and no self-duality is inferred from the head alone. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 6.1, given] ∎

items.title: The degenerate Ariki theorem does not imply the nondegenerate one
items.statement:
**Refuted claim:** the characteristic-zero generic comparison between the
integrally charged degenerate tower and the nondegenerate tower can be
specialized to every nonzero Hecke parameter, thereby transporting the
degenerate Ariki theorem to every nondegenerate parameter without further
comparison results.

Already over $\mathbb C$, at level one, charge $m\in\mathbb Z$ and rank two,
the full degenerate algebra is $\mathbb C[S_2]$, whereas the nondegenerate
algebra at $\xi=-1$ is $\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. They have two
and one simple modules, respectively, and are not isomorphic. Thus the
claimed universal algebra transport is false. This refutes the proposed
method of inference; it does not assert that the nondegenerate Ariki theorem
itself is false or cannot be proved using additional results.

The genuine generic comparison and generic categorification equivalence
remain in their characteristic-zero, infinite-order, integral-charge scope,
as recorded in
[[rem-degenerate-and-nondegenerate-ariki-theorems-have-distinct-parameter-ranges]].
The full generic based/tower branch remains dependent on the coherent
comparison and standard-class dictionary, rather than on unrelated
rankwise algebra isomorphisms alone.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] The quadratic Hecke relation in
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] is $(T_r-\xi)(T_r+1)=0$.
At rank two there is one generator and no braid relation.

[F2] The defining relations of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] at rank two are
$s^2=1$, $x_1x_2=x_2x_1$, $sx_2=x_1s+1$ and $x_2s=sx_1+1$.
The level-one quotient of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] imposes
$x_1=m$. Only these defining relations, not its tensor-realization proof,
are needed below.

[F3] In the nondegenerate affine presentation of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]],
$X_1,X_2$ are commuting units and $TX_1T=\xi X_2$, in addition to [F1].
Its monic level-one cyclotomic quotient imposes $X_1=Q$.

## Counterexample

**Given:** The rank-two presentations of [F1]-[F3] over $\mathbb C$,
level one and integral charge $m$. The nondegenerate cyclotomic root is
$Q=\xi^m$; we verify its reduction to the finite Hecke presentation below.
We test universal specialization of the generic algebra transport.

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 In the degenerate quotient $x_1=m$ and $sx_2=ms+1$ give $x_2=m+s$. Hence the quotient is generated by $s$ with $s^2=1$. Conversely the assignments $x_1\mapsto m$, $x_2\mapsto m+s$, $s\mapsto s$ in $\mathbb C[s]/(s^2-1)$ satisfy both cross relations and commutativity, so they define an inverse to the map sending $s$ into the quotient. Evaluation at $s=1,-1$ identifies this algebra with $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, with inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(a+b)/2+(a-b)s/2$. In particular it has no nonzero nilpotents and has precisely the two one-dimensional simple modules $s=1,-1$. [F2, algebra, construct]

1.2 In the nondegenerate level-one quotient [F3], $X_1=Q$ and $X_2=Q\xi^{-1}T^2$, so it is generated by $T$. Conversely in the finite algebra $H_\xi(2)$ of [F1], $T^{-1}=\xi^{-1}(T-(\xi-1))$. The assignments $X_1\mapsto Q$, $X_2\mapsto Q\xi^{-1}T^2$, $T\mapsto T$ therefore give commuting units satisfying $TX_1T=\xi X_2$ and the cyclotomic relation. They define the inverse of the map from $H_\xi(2)$ into the quotient: both composites fix $T,X_1,X_2$ and their inverses. Hence the whole nondegenerate level-one rank-two quotient is exactly $H_\xi(2)$ for every $\xi\ne0$ and $Q=\xi^m$. This uses only the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions, not a finite-$e$ theorem in the generic branch. [F1, F3, algebra, construct]

2.1 At $\xi=-1$, step 1.2 and [F1] give $H_{-1}(2)=\mathbb C[T]/((T+1)^2)$. Setting $\varepsilon=T+1$ identifies it with $B=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$, whose basis is $1,\varepsilon$ by division by the monic polynomial $\varepsilon^2$. Thus $\varepsilon$ is nonzero and nilpotent. Every $a+b\varepsilon$ with $a\ne0$ has inverse $a^{-1}-ba^{-2}\varepsilon$; those with $a=0$ are nonunits. Consequently $(\varepsilon)$ is the unique maximal ideal and is the nonzero radical. Every simple $B$-module is killed by $\varepsilon$: its image under this central operator is a submodule, and if the image were the whole nonzero simple module, its square could not vanish. The unique simple is therefore $B/(\varepsilon)\cong\mathbb C$. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 At rank two the limitation can be seen in an actual comparison formula. For $\xi\ne-1$ put $a=(\xi-1)/2$ and $b=(\xi+1)/2$. The map $T\mapsto a+bs$ respects [F1] because its values at $s=1,-1$ are $\xi,-1$; its inverse is $s\mapsto(T-a)/b$, since the quadratic relation implies $(T-a)^2=b^2$. At $\xi=-1$ this inverse is undefined and the specialized map sends $T$ to $-1$, killing the nonzero element $T+1$. This explicit generic comparison therefore does not specialize to an isomorphism. Other rank-two parameters can yield isomorphisms, including some roots of unity; that does not repair the universal assertion. [F1, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

3.1 The two algebras cannot be isomorphic: an isomorphism would send the nonzero square-zero element of step 2.1 to a nonzero nilpotent in the algebra of step 1.1. Their decomposition behavior also differs directly. The regular module of $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$ is the direct sum of its two simples. The regular module $B$ has the filtration $0\subset(\varepsilon)\subset B$ with both subquotients equal to its unique simple; it is indecomposable since an idempotent $a+b\varepsilon$ satisfies $a^2=a$ and $2ab=b$, forcing it to be $0$ or $1$. Thus even projective and simple classes cannot be identified across these two specializations by algebra transport. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 disprove the claimed universal algebra transport and step 2.2 exhibits its failure in a concrete comparison formula. The witness uses the entire rank-two algebras, with the degenerate full integer residue set; it is not a comparison with a supported cut retaining only the charge $m$. For a finite degenerate cut containing this entire example the root interval must contain $m-1,m,m+1$, since $x_2=m\pm1$ on its two simples. The calculation is choice-free and entirely over $\mathbb C$. It neither extends characteristic-zero canonical-basis identifications to positive characteristic nor replaces the separate root-of-unity comparison and grading theorems. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra, given] ∎
